 Order

The present petitioner under Article 226 of the Constitution of India has been preferred against the order dated 24.03.2023 issued by the DEO, District Gwalior, whereby the petitioner has been placed under suspension as the marksheet of Diploma on the basis of which he had sought appointment has been found to be forged.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that with regard to some cause of action a criminal case was registered against the petitioner under Section 420, 467, 468, 471 of IPC and the said criminal case was quashed in MCRC No.3547/2022 vide order dated 23.03.2022 and, therefore,
since the very cause of action on the basis of which the petitioner was placed under suspension has Anish Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169204930/
1 come to an end, nothing survives in the matter and the order of suspension passed by the competent authority needs to be recalled and revoked.
Per contra, shri G.K. Agarwal, learned Government Advocate appearing on advance copy submits that against the order of suspension, the petitioner is having an alternative efficacious remedy available under Rule 23 of the MPCCA Rules, 1966, therefore, the present petition is not maintainable.

entities.text: Anish Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, he prays for dismissal of the present petition.
Heard the counsels for the parties and perused the record.
Admittedly, the petitioner is assailing his order of suspension dated 24.03.2023, against which an appeal lies under Rule 23 of the MPCCA Rules, 1966.

It is not the case of the petitioner that the said remedy is not available to him or the authority who is to hear the appeal has passed the suspension order nor it is the case of the petitioner that it is against the principles of natural justice.
Thus, looking to the alternative and efficacious remedy available to the petitioner under Rule 23 of the MPCCA Rules, 1966, the petitioner is directed to avail the remedy available to him as per law.
In the light of the aforesaid, the petition stands disposed of.
